subject: English 1st Paper

source.edition: Revised for the year 2026; revised edition October 2025

passagePolicy: Use the specifically cited source section in the NCTB textbook. Full textbook passages and images are not reproduced. Original writing models are not source facts.

activities.instruction: Answer using the cited text. Equivalent accurate wording is acceptable; support interpretations with details.

items.question: What is the title of the poem in Section A?
Who is credited as the author of the abridged poem?
What difficulty with English does the poem illustrate?
items.modelAnswer: It illustrates that similar spellings can have different pronunciations and that spelling alone does not reliably predict every sound.

items.question: How do the many contrasting word examples help the poem’s purpose?
items.modelAnswer: They let readers notice and practise pronunciation differences rather than only being told that English is difficult.

items.question: What tone does the poem create? Give a reason.
items.modelAnswer: It creates a playful, humorous tone by presenting a crowded series of tricky words and joking about the speaker’s struggles.

items.question: What contrast does the ending make between speaking and writing?
items.modelAnswer: The speaker says that he learned to speak when young but still had difficulty writing much later. This is part of the poem’s humorous voice, not a verified biography.

items.question: Why should learners not assume similar-looking words always rhyme?
items.modelAnswer: The poem gives groups with similar spellings but different sounds, showing why pronunciation must be checked and practised.

items.question: What shared vowel sound do the printed words alive, five and write practise in A2?
items.modelAnswer: They practise the diphthong /aɪ/, as in five.

activities.instruction: Explain the word in the cited context, or give the requested alternative meaning. Accept suitable equivalent wording.

acceptedAnswers: make a mistake or have difficulty while saying the words
have the same or similar ending sound
the land along the edge of a sea or other body of water

activities.instruction: Write three sentences describing how you can practise unfamiliar English words.
activities.modelAnswer: I can check an unfamiliar word in a reliable dictionary. I can listen to a trusted pronunciation model and practise saying it. I can compare the word with a similar-looking word instead of assuming they sound the same.
activities.note: Original study advice. Reading these answers does not measure spoken pronunciation; teacher observation or audio practice remains necessary.
